p.i: valde multa funt, quas tamen praecipue oculis notare possumus inter fixas Astronomi in certas figuras seu constellationes redegerunt.

main_text.p: §. 1. Astronomorum diligentia in illis stellis digerendis nota est, quod nempe stellas fixas omnes in 48. asterismos seu imagines tribuerint, & eas quae notantur numero 1022. descripserint, quibus Nautae ad auftrum aliquot adjunxerunt. Ordo & nomina iftarum imaginum his versibus includuntur:

l.i: Ad borea partes ter septe fidera cernes, Arcti, Draco, Bootes, Gemma Corona, Genuquc
Pegasus, & Delphin, Telum, hinc Aquila, Anguitenenfque
Signifer inde subeft, bis sex, qui fidera complet.
Sunt Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo,
Libraque, Scorpius, Arcitenens, Caper, Amphora, Pisces.
Post ter quinque tibi signa haec vertuntur ad auftrum.
Catus, & Eridanus, Lepus, & nimbofus Orion, Syrius,

page.notes: Lower lines of the verse are partly cut off at the foot of the page; the last word of the verse is read as printed. Some words in the verse are doubtful, e.g. "Genuquc" and "Catus", which may be read as Genuque and Cetus; the verse is printed as seen. The Greek-letter style of "&" marks are roman ampersands.
